text:
emma: Heads up — noticed a bunch of negative partner commission lines in the March payout export for ChannelPartner Inc. Can someone check why proration produced refunds instead of normal commissions?
raj: Which export? CSV from our payouts job or vendor reconciliation feed?
emma: The payouts CSV from billing-run-2026-03-31, attached excerpt below. Looks like we applied mid-cycle seat decreases but the customer actually upgraded.
jordan: Oof, that sounds like a SKU stacking/proration edge case we saw in Q4 but for upgrades. Can you paste the lines?
emma: Sure — here's the minimal snippet we pulled from the payout file:```
sku,customer_id,period_start,period_end,quantity,unit_price,total,commission_rate,partner_revenue
redwood-pro-monthly,ACCT-993,2026-03-01,2026-03-31,3,100,300,0.20,60
redwood-pro-monthly,ACCT-993,2026-03-15,2026-03-31,-1,100,-100,0.20,-20
redwood-pro-monthly,ACCT-993,2026-03-20,2026-03-31,2,100,200,0.20,40
```
emma: The net quantity is 4 seats billed, but we have that -1 line causing a negative partner_revenue (-20) which pushed their monthly payout negative once aggregated with other customers.
mike: That -1 line usually comes from the proration delta when a seat is transferred between SKUs during a mid-cycle change. Our aggregator should coalesce deltas per customer per sku before computing partner cuts.
raj: Is this only ChannelPartner Inc or wider? Any other partners flagged?
emma: I scanned the March feed; there are ~12 partners with small negative deltas, and ChannelPartner Inc is the largest hit (~-$1.2k).
jordan: @laura can you confirm if ChannelPartner reported any ticket? Partner AMs might have flagged it already.
laura: I saw a ping earlier from them — they named an invoice ID (INV-73321) but thought it was a customer refund. They asked why partner payout was reduced. I replied we'd investigate.
finance-bot: Automated check: payout-2026-03-31.csv processed; anomalies detected: 12 partners with negative net partner_revenue after aggregation. See /internal/reports/payout-anomalies/2026-03-31
mike: Root cause hypothesis: our Billing Aggregator (v2) is summing partner_revenue across line items without normalizing proration entries that should be netted prior to commission calc. The legacy pipeline netted deltas first.
raj: Can we reproduce locally? Mike, can you run the aggregator for ACCT-993 for March and share the diff vs legacy?
mike: On it. ETA 45m. Will run with `python tools/agg_recompute.py --account ACCT-993 --period 2026-03` and attach output.
emma: Also: please don't surface any partner-facing numbers until we confirm. We should prepare a short customer-facing explanation if we need to issue a top-up.
jordan: If it's a processing bug, we might need to create retro adjustment for partners and notify partners + partners team. Possible scope: March only or Jan-Mar depending on when v2 deployed. When did v2 roll out?
raj: v2 rolled to production 2026-02-10 for marketplace and 2026-02-20 for channel. So check Feb as well.
mike: Recompute done. Diff summary: legacy partner_revenue = $80 for ACCT-993; v2 pipeline = -$20. Breakdown attached (pasted):```
legacy_net_quantity:4
legacy_partner_revenue:80
v2_line_sum_partner_revenue: -20
root_cause: proration lines not normalized before partner cut
```
mike: Confirmed bug in v2: it applies `commission_rate` per line and then sums, which creates the negative. Legacy applied commission to neted quantity.
raj: Next steps: 1) Run full reconciliation for Feb+Mar across all partners and flag > $100 corrections. 2) Generate retro adjustments for affected partners 3) Draft partner communication + Q&A 4) Hotfix v2 to mirror legacy net-first behaviour. Assign owners?
emma: I'll own partner comms + approvals for adjustments. Jordan, you'll own partner outreach and list.
jordan: Yep, I'll get the partner list. @mike please prioritize hotfix and a test case to prevent regressions.
mike: I can push a patch to billing-aggregator today; will open PR and request review from eng-platform. PR link will be posted when ready.
raj: I'll run the reconciliation job after your patch merges and produce an adjustments spreadsheet for Finance sign-off.
laura: I'll draft the message template: short apology, what happened, what we'll do (top-up + statement), ETA 5 business days.
emma: Thanks. Please also include a sample invoice blurb we can attach.
mike: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/p/billing-aggregator/pull/459 — patch adds netting step before commission calc and unit test.
jordan: Great. Raj, any blockers running reconciliation?
raj: Need a small compute window; finance approval to re-run March job and generate <adjustments.csv>. Emma, approve?
emma: Approved — proceed. Please tag me on the adjustments sheet and put total adjustments under $10k in the single approval bucket; anything larger needs CFO sign-off.
raj: Understood. Kicking off run now.
finance-bot: Job started: payout-recompute-2026-03 (job id 8a7f). Progress logs: /logs/payout-recompute/8a7f
laura: I'll prep partner comms draft and loop Emma before sending.
mike: Quick note for postmortem: add a regression test for stacked SKU proration scenarios (increase, decrease, transfer) to CI.
emma: Agreed. Also add a short blameless summary for incident tracker.
jordan: I'll create the Jira for partner adjustments and link PR + recon run. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-5123
emma: Thanks everyone. Please update this thread when recon completes or if numbers change.
raj: Recon finished. Summary: 9 partners affected, total partner top-ups = $7,820. Adjustment CSV uploaded: /internal/finance/adjustments/adj-2026-03-31.csv.
jordan: Uploading partner notifications to the draft folder and syncing with Partners team.
laura: Message ready, will send after Emma sign-off.
emma: Sign-off sent. Send out tomorrow morning PST.
finance-bot: Adjustment processed: payout-topup-batch-2311368342 completed. Partners will see credits in next payout cycle.
emma: Closing action: document change in billing runbook and mark incident FIN-5123 resolved after postmortem. Good catch, team :thumbsup:
